summary: Ustaz Azlan tells of the physical and mental torture of the weak and unprotected in Makkah, starting with Ibn Mas'ud's hadith on the first seven to make their Islam public. He recounts Bilal ibn Rabah, who kept saying 'Ahad, Ahad' and was freed by Abu Bakr; enslaved women such as Zinnirah and An-Nahdiyah; Khabbab ibn Al-Aratt, whose back was burnt; Suhayb Ar-Rumi, who gave up his wealth to emigrate; and the family of Yasir and Ammar, where Sumayyah and Yasir were martyred and Ammar was permitted to say what was demanded while his heart stayed firm. He links this to suffering in Gaza, the Rohingya and a bullying death in Malaysia, and closes with verses of Al-Ankabut and Al-Baqarah on trial and a warning against haste.
keyPoints: The first seven to make their Islam public were the Prophet SAW, Abu Bakr, Ammar, his mother Sumayyah, Suhayb and Bilal; the Prophet SAW and Abu Bakr were protected by their clans.
Bilal was tortured with armour and a boulder but only repeated 'Ahad, Ahad', then Abu Bakr bought and freed him.
Allah affirmed Abu Bakr's sincerity in Surah Al-Layl 18-21 when he was accused of hidden agendas.
Khabbab's back was burnt through yet he kept teaching Quran and later showed it to Umar.
Suhayb surrendered all his wealth to emigrate and was welcomed by the Prophet SAW as a profitable trade.
Sumayyah and Yasir were the first martyrs; Ammar was permitted to utter disbelief under duress while his heart was at peace with faith.
Victory cannot be chased in haste and trials will come to everyone who claims faith.

lessons.title: Sirah demands action
lessons.body: Reading sirah with one eye only is a mistake; it demands readiness to sacrifice.

lessons.title: Allah does not forget unknown sacrifices
lessons.body: Even if people do not know their names, the reward and the oppressors' wrongs are reckoned.

lessons.title: Faith lodged in the heart
lessons.body: Bilal held to one word; true belief is seen in hardship, not in religious exam marks.

lessons.title: Du'a must come with action
lessons.body: Du'a is a weapon but must not be an excuse to abandon responsibility.

lessons.title: Sincerity needs no defence
lessons.body: Allah affirmed Abu Bakr's sincerity though he was accused of hidden agendas.

lessons.title: Companions prized sacrifice
lessons.body: They boasted of how many slaves they freed, not degrees.

lessons.title: The freed lived alongside oppressors
lessons.body: Survivors lived for years beside perpetrators without being able to report.

lessons.title: Accept calamity with words that please Allah
lessons.body: Parents who forgive and avoid words that anger Allah are models of faith.

lessons.title: Victory cannot be hunted
lessons.body: Do not pray to see your own victory; many strivers died without seeing the result.

lessons.title: Ego in choosing role models
lessons.body: We tend to pick companions who won in this world, not those who endured like Sumayyah.

lessons.title: Beware the disease of wahn
lessons.body: Love of the world and fear of death make the ummah numerous yet weak.

lessons.title: Honour those who struggled
lessons.body: Today's blessings come from unknown struggles; study history and do not rely on short clips.

dalil.context: Ibn Mas'ud's hadith, stated by the ustaz to be authentic in Sunan Ibn Majah.
dalil.translation: The first seven to make Islam public were the Messenger of Allah SAW, Abu Bakr, Ammar and his mother Sumayyah, Suhayb and Bilal; Allah protected the Prophet SAW through his uncle and Abu Bakr through his people, while the others were put in armour and left in the heat, except Bilal who valued himself little for Allah.

dalil.context: Bilal's reward after his torture and the first adhan he called.
dalil.translation: I heard the sound of Bilal's footsteps in Paradise.

dalil.context: The one who gives his wealth to purify himself.
dalil.translation: who gives his wealth away as self-purification,

dalil.context: He owes no favour that must be repaid.
dalil.translation: not to return a favour to anyone

dalil.context: Only seeking the pleasure of his Lord, the Most High.
dalil.translation: but for the sake of his Lord the Most High––

dalil.context: He will surely be satisfied with Allah's reward.
dalil.translation: and he will be well pleased.

dalil.context: An example of accepting calamity with words pleasing to Allah.
dalil.translation: This is mercy; the eye weeps and the heart grieves, but we say only what pleases our Lord.

dalil.context: The Prophet SAW passed by Yasir's family under torture and could only give a promise.
dalil.translation: Be patient, O family of Yasir, for your promised place is Paradise.

dalil.context: A concession for those forced to utter disbelief.
dalil.translation: The Prophet SAW asked Ammar how he found his heart; he said at peace with faith; the Prophet SAW said, if they return, then repeat it.

dalil.context: The verse that came down in defence of Ammar: except one who is compelled while his heart is at peace with faith.
dalil.translation: With the exception of those who are forced to say they do not believe, although their hearts remain firm in faith, those who reject God after believing in Him and open their hearts to disbelief will have the wrath of God upon them and a grievous punishment awaiting them.

dalil.context: A motivation to be patient, not a sign the Prophet SAW lacked compassion.
dalil.translation: Khabbab asked why the Prophet SAW did not seek help for them; he replied that earlier peoples were seized, sawn in two or combed with iron combs yet did not turn from their religion; Allah will complete this matter, but you are impatient.

dalil.context: Do people think they will be left alone saying 'we believe' without being tested?
Do you think you will enter Paradise before the trials that came to earlier peoples?
dalil.translation: Do you suppose that you will enter the Garden without first having suffered like those before you? They were afflicted by misfortune and hardship, and they were so shaken that even [their] messenger and the believers with him cried, ‘When will God’s help arrive?’ Truly, God’s help is near.

dalil.context: Why the ummah is weak despite being numerous and rich.
dalil.translation: You will be many but like foam on the sea, afflicted with wahn, love of the world and fear of death.
